chapter: Trummy Young's band, 52nd Street and the Navy
title: Kelly's Stables recordings and the White Roses bar
summary: He recalls a Hawkins-Gillespie record with Leo Parker and the bar where musicians mingled between sets.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I remember one time Coleman Hawkins had a band in a place called Kelly's Stables. Once they recorded this thing with Dizzy Gillespie, and I remember Leo Parker was playing alto saxophone on that. "Disorder At The Border" -- there were four sides they did, I think.

There was just music everywhere. Moreso, there were musicians that you could actually, between sets, go around to a bar they had called the White Roses where everybody congregated, and guys would go around there and just drink. And you know, standing next to Art Tatum or whomever, or shaking hands with this one and saying "Hello" to this one... For a young musician, you really felt like you were into something.
